<a id="domain-external"></a>

# external

In [EhosContract.Domain](domain-dsl.md), section `domain`.

```elixir
external name, label
```

An external system, named after what it does for the business, not after the vendor.

**Arguments**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| `name` | `atom` | yes |  | The external's name. |
| `label` | `String.t` | yes |  | What the business calls it. |

**Options**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| `direction` | `:inbound \| :outbound \| :bidirectional` | yes |  | Which way data flows. |
| `unavailable_looks_like` | `String.t` |  |  | How an outage shows to the business. |
| `expected_latency` | `any` |  |  | How long an answer usually takes, `{n, unit}`. |
| `source` | `String.t` |  |  | Where the external comes from in the material. |

Inside it: [`operation`](#domain-external-operation).

<a id="domain-external-operation"></a>

## external.operation

```elixir
operation name, label
```

What the system does when an effect calls it; once a system declares one, every `calls:` to it names one, `calls: {:p1, :submit_report}`.

**Arguments**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| `name` | `atom` | yes |  | The operation's name. |
| `label` | `String.t` | yes |  | What it does, as the business says it. |

**Options**

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Docs |
|------|------|----------|---------|------|
| `source` | `String.t` |  |  | Where the operation comes from in the material. |
